purpose: ASVS V1.3.12. A regular expression written down in the source can be parsed and checked for the shapes that cause exponential backtracking, and scripts/security/verify-regex-backtracking.mjs does that for every one of them. A regular expression built from a value cannot be: what it ends up being depends on what reaches the value at run time. Those sites are recorded here instead, each with what can reach the interpolated value and why that cannot introduce a quantifier the sweep would have rejected. The sweep fails on a site that is not recorded and on a recorded site that no longer exists, so this file cannot quietly fall behind the tree.
identity: A site is identified by its file and the expression compiled, not by line number: moving code keeps the judgement, changing what gets compiled asks for it again.
note: The instance this requirement grew out of was exactly this shape - a key taken from a request and compiled into a per-key RegExp, where a key of (.*)*x did not finish against an ordinary 1901-character contract in 120 seconds. The question each entry has to answer is therefore not 'is this pattern safe today' but 'can anything outside the repository decide what this pattern is'.

sites.why: match[1] is a capture from the literal alternation (think(?:ing)?|analysis|reasoning|scratchpad|tool(?:[_ -]?(?:call|calls|trace))?|debug) a few lines above, so it can only ever be one of those words. Model output decides which one, never the characters: no metacharacter can reach the closing-tag pattern.

ru() expands three shorthands in a literal string argument: \w* becomes [\p{L}\p{N}]*, \_? becomes [\s,]* and \_ becomes [\s,]+. Every argument is a literal in this module, so the eight resulting patterns are fixed. They matter more than most - they run on assistant chat input - so all eight were resolved and analysed: none carries an exponential shape, and each stays flat (about 1-3ms, falling as it warms) against runs of up to 1600 characters that do not match. What they do carry is the mild adjacency [\p{L}\p{N}]* followed by [\s,]+, which the sweep reports as polynomial and does not fail on.

term is escaped at the call, and the only other variable part is a choice between one literal and the empty string. The surrounding shape has no quantifier over a group, so the one unbounded piece cannot be repeated.

escaped is the fragment with every metacharacter escaped on the line above. The lookarounds are zero-width and there is no quantifier over a group.
